newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines okays 7.6 bln pesos debt notes issue.
newsitem.headline: Philippines okays 7.6 bln pesos debt notes issue.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday it had approved applications from four firms to issue 7.6 billion pesos worth of commercial papers.

The SEC said among the debt paper applications approved were the proposed two-billion peso long term commercial papers of Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a member of the Royal Dutch Shell group, and the three-billion peso long term commercial papers of mass housing builder C & P Homes Inc.

The SEC also approved the applications of holding firm Metro Pacific Corp to renew its permit to float one-billion pesos worth of short term commercial papers and the planned 1.6-billion peso short term float of PCI Leasing and Finance Inc, a unit of Philippine Commercial International Bank.
The Shell debt papers will be issued in two tranches, with four or five-year maturities.

The SEC said the debt notes of Shell will be based on the applicable base rate of the 91-day Philippine treasury bill plus a spread of 0.625 percent annually for the four-year maturities, and a spread of 0.75 percent annually for five year maturities.
The yield on the C & P papers will be based on the 91-day treasury bill rates plus one percent for five-year maturities and 1.125 percent for seven year maturities.
The debt papers of MPC and PCI Leasing will both mature in a year. Applicable yields on the papers were not indicated.
